<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   - This is a backend “Realtime” server built in Elixir/Phoenix. It exposes:
     • A REST API to manage tenants and extensions  
     • A WebSocket API (Phoenix Channels) for Broadcast, Presence, and Postgres-CDC events  
   - It also includes a “demo” Next.js front-end showing how clients consume Broadcast/Presence/CDC.

2. Analyze the file structure  
   - Top-level: mix.exs, config/, lib/, priv/, releases (rel/), Docker, CI workflows  
   - lib/realtime: core OTP application (adapters, CDC, subscription management, rate counters, tenants)  
   - lib/extensions/postgres_cdc_rls: custom Postgres-CDC + RLS logic  
   - lib/realtime_web: Phoenix endpoint, controllers (HTTP API), plugs, channels (WebSocket logic), LiveView inspector, telemetry/metrics  
   - demo/: standalone Next.js/React/TypeScript app using @supabase/realtime-js  
   - priv/repo + lib/realtime/tenants: multi-tenant migrations, seeds  
   - deploy/, docker-compose.yml: container/deployment configs  

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   - Confirms the three core features: Broadcast, Presence, Postgres Changes via WAL2JSON CDC  
   - Describes environment variables, JWT-based tenant auth, cluster/telemetry settings  
   - Points to “demo” folder as example client  

4. Main components and interactions  
   a. Clients  
     - WebSocket clients (browser/mobile) using JWT to authenticate  
     - REST clients for tenant CRUD  
     - Demo Next.js app (demo/)  
   b. API Layer (HTTP)  
     - Phoenix Controllers under realtime_web/controllers  
     - Exposes `/api/tenants` for tenant management  
   c. WebSocket Layer  
     - Phoenix Endpoint (realtime_web/endpoint.ex)  
     - Channels: Broadcast, Presence, RealtimeChannel (+ authorization plugs)  
   d. Subscription Manager & CDC Extension  
     - lib/extensions/postgres_cdc_rls: polls WAL, applies RLS, produces change events  
     - SubscriptionSupervisor spawns per-tenant pollers  
   e. Message Dispatcher & PubSub  
     - Routes inbound client messages + CDC events to channel handlers  
     - Phoenix.PubSub for fan-out across nodes  
   f. Multi-tenancy  
     - Global management DB (`_realtime.tenants`, `_realtime.extensions`)  
     - Dynamic Supervisors spawn tenant-scoped processes (connections, counters, janitors)  
   g. Cluster Infrastructure  
     - gen_rpc for inter-node RPC (metrics collection, process inspection)  
     - ClusterStrategy (Postgres-based) for node discovery  
   h. Database(s)  
     - Global Postgres for tenant metadata  
     - Tenant Postgres(s)/schemas for CDC and RLS  
     - Migrations under priv/repo & realtime/tenants/repo  
   i. Monitoring & Telemetry  
     - PromEx plugins for channels, gen_rpc, OS metrics, Erlang VM metrics  
     - Exposes `/metrics` HTTP endpoint  

5. Relationships and data flow  
   - Client → HTTP API: create/read tenants, fetch JWT secrets  
   - Client → WebSocket: connect to `/socket`, authenticate via JWT  
   - WebSocket → join channels → subscription manager → start CDC poller  
   - CDC poller → WAL JSON events → subscription manager → Phoenix.PubSub → client channel  
   - Client events (broadcast/presence) → channel handlers → MessageDispatcher → PubSub → peers  
   - Node-to-node (gen_rpc) → forward cluster metrics, sync processes  
   - Phoenix → Ecto Repo → Postgres for metadata + RLS enforcement  

6. Architectural patterns and design principles  
   - OTP Supervision Tree with dynamic supervisors per tenant  
   - Adapter pattern for supporting multiple CDC protocols  
   - MVC for HTTP, Channels for WebSocket  
   - PubSub for decoupled message broadcast  
   - Row-Level Security in Postgres for channel authorization  
   - Layered: API → Business Logic → Adapters → Database  
   - Multi-tenant isolation via separate DB connections/schemas  

7. Diagram guidelines  
   - Use clear labels (e.g., “WebSocket Clients,” “Phoenix Endpoint,” “CDC Poller”)  
   - Directional arrows for:  
     • HTTP calls  
     • WebSocket connect/join  
     • DB queries/CDC stream  
     • PubSub message flow  
   - Color coding:  
     • Blue: Clients & Demo Front-end  
     • Green: API/WebSocket Layer  
     • Orange: Core Business Logic & Adapters  
     • Gray: Databases  
     • Purple: Cluster/Inter-node  
   - Shapes:  
     • Cylinders for Databases  
     • Rectangles for Services/Modules  
     • Clouds for External/Monitoring services (Prometheus, Opentelemetry)  
   - Show grouping for per-tenant processes under a “Tenant Supervisor” box  

8. Tailoring to this project  
   - Emphasize the multi-tenant CDC pipeline and RLS extension  
   - Highlight the dual-role of the Phoenix app (HTTP + WebSocket)  
   - Show demo/Next.js client consuming Broadcast/Presence/CDC via @supabase/realtime-js  
   - Display cluster communication via gen_rpc  

9. Final checklist for diagram  
   - Component labels  
   - Arrows indicating data flow and dependencies  
   - Legend for colors/shapes  
   - Detailed enough to show API layer, WebSocket layer, CDC adapter, multi-tenant supervisors, cluster bus, databases, and monitoring  
</explanation>
